$comment: How each spec failure_taxonomy category becomes a SystemVerilog assertion. This file is the reviewable CATALOG: which command pair a rule constrains, which spec timing parameter bounds it, and whether the bank must match. The cycle counts are NOT here — they are computed at generation time from the spec's nanosecond values and the controller clock period, so a spec change changes the assertions without editing this file.
$unit_note: Cycle counts are derived as ceil(param_ns / controller_clock_period_ns). The spec's $derived_cycles are expressed in nCK (DDR clocks, tCK=1.25ns) while commands are issued on the controller clock (5.0ns); deriving from nanoseconds avoids that unit mismatch entirely and states the physical requirement the standard actually imposes.
$independence_note: These assertions count elapsed cycles from the OBSERVED command stream. They deliberately do not reference the design's own timing counters or permission signals. bank_tracker.sv already contains assertions of the form 'cmd_rd_valid |-> (ctr_rcd[bank] == 0)', which check the design against its own counter: if the counter is loaded wrongly, the assertion agrees with the bug. An independent check must recompute the requirement from the spec.

command_signals.$precharge_all_note: JESD79-3: a PRECHARGE with A10 high precharges every bank, not just the addressed one. Bank-state tracking that ignores this leaves banks marked open after they were closed, and the protocol assertions then fire on correct behaviour — the exact failure mode that teaches people to ignore assertions.

min_separation_rules.requirement: READ or WRITE issued before tRCD elapsed after ACTIVATE to same bank.
ACTIVATE issued before tRP elapsed after PRECHARGE to same bank.
PRECHARGE issued before tRAS elapsed after ACTIVATE to same bank.
ACTIVATE issued before tRC elapsed after previous ACTIVATE to same bank.
ACTIVATE to different bank before tRRD elapsed.
READ issued before tWTR elapsed after last WRITE data burst.
PRECHARGE issued before tWR elapsed after last WRITE data burst.
PRECHARGE issued before tRTP elapsed after READ command.
Command issued before tRFC elapsed after REFRESH.

window_rules.note: A sliding-window count, not a pairwise separation: generated as a shift register over the window and a population count.

state_rules.requirement: READ/WRITE issued to a bank that has no active row.
state_rules.note: Row-open state is tracked HERE from observed ACT/PRE commands, never read from the design's own bank state, so a wrong state machine cannot excuse itself.

state_rules.requirement: ACTIVATE issued to a bank that already has an active row without intervening PRECHARGE.

proposed_taxonomy_extensions.$why: The taxonomy bounds every timing parameter except tREFI. tREFI is a MAXIMUM interval, not a minimum separation, so it needs its own rule kind; JESD79-3 allows up to max_postpone_count refreshes to be deferred, so the observable bound is (max_postpone_count + 1) x tREFI between REFRESH commands.
proposed_taxonomy_extensions.TIMING_012: tREFI violation: no REFRESH issued within (max_postpone_count + 1) x tREFI of the previous REFRESH.

max_interval_rules.requirement: No REFRESH issued within (max_postpone_count + 1) x tREFI of the previous REFRESH.
max_interval_rules.note: Armed by the first observed REFRESH (the window before it belongs to initialisation, whose length init_fsm decides). One error per missed interval: the assertion fires on the cycle the gap first exceeds the bound, not on every cycle after.

command_groups.name: init
command_groups.$why: The init FSM issues its own command stream (init_cmd) before cmd_gen owns the pins. Its inter-step delays are INIT_002; the spec states tZQinit (initialization_sequence.tZQinit_ns) — tMRD and tMOD are NOT in the spec, so MRS-to-MRS spacing cannot be asserted (intake rule INIT_TMRD/INIT_TMOD).

min_separation_rules.requirement: Insufficient delay between init sequence steps: a command issued before tZQinit elapsed after ZQCL.
